Group strains with identical profiles

Source: R/define_profiles.R
define_profiles.Rd

Concatenates the columns of the binary table into one profile per strain and gives the same group number to strains with identical profiles.

Usage

define_profiles(data, sep = "")

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per strain, typically the binary table returned by prepare_upset().

sep

Separator used between values when building the profiles (none by default).

Value

A data frame with the same row names as data and three columns:

profiles

the profile of the strain (concatenated values);

group

an integer identifying the group of identical profiles;

names

the strain identifier.

See also

Other profile method: prepare_upset(), select_profiles(), select_strains()

Examples

raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
#> no duplicate ID
#> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE
upset_data <- prepare_upset(prepared_data)
upset_profiles <- define_profiles(upset_data)
# number of distinct profiles
max(upset_profiles$group)
#> [1] 61
